sources.entry: BitSpring - Open-source bit-perfect music player with native DSD, per-track sample rates up to 768 kHz and AutoEQ headphone EQ. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/crash2bash/bitspring) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: BitSpring
summary.one_liner: BitSpring is a free, open-source bit-perfect music player for macOS, Windows, Linux and Android that sends audio to the DAC without resampling or system mixing.
use_cases: play high-resolution FLAC or ALAC files to a USB DAC without resampling
play DSD albums natively over DoP or as PCM
stream lossless music to Sonos, WiiM or Chromecast devices
even out loudness between tracks with ReplayGain-style levelling
upsample audio to 192, 384 or 768 kHz for a DAC
summary.what_it_does: BitSpring plays local music files and takes exclusive control of the output device so the DAC receives the file's samples unchanged. On macOS it uses CoreAudio hog mode, on Windows WASAPI Exclusive, on Linux direct ALSA access, and on Android 14 and later a bit-perfect USB path. It switches the DAC to each track's sample rate and says so when it has to resample. DSD (DSF, DFF, SACD ISO) plays over DoP or as 176.4 kHz PCM. Optional enhancers (off by default) include upsampling with several filters, AutoEQ/Equalizer APO/EasyEffects EQ import, crossfeed, MP3/AAC headroom handling, and volume levelling towards -18 LUFS. A main screen shows file format, DAC rate and active processing steps.
notable: Open source under the MIT licence, code on GitHub
Bit-perfect indicator switches to 'Processing' when any enhancer is active
Native DSD playback over DoP up to DSD1024
Streams to UPnP/DLNA and Google Cast devices as lossless FLAC
caveats: Bit-perfect exclusive output blocks other apps from using the DAC while BitSpring holds it
Bit-perfect USB path on Android requires Android 14 or later; older versions use the system mixer
If the DAC cannot match a track's sample rate, audio is resampled
